title: Targeted Region Evacuation and Phased Rollback Runbook for Mixed Hosted/Dedicated Incidents
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: Provide an operator-focused, minimum-friction runbook for evacuating traffic away from a single-region or partial-region failure that impacts both Hosted and Dedicated customers. Scope includes: stepwise traffic quarantine, tenant-aware routing decisions, KV cache reconciliation checks, safe-fallback to lower-capacity model variants, and pre-approved customer communications. This runbook emphasizes incremental evacuation (node->rack->region slices) to avoid wholesale rollbacks and minimize customer-visible errors.
steps: 1) Initial assessment: Confirm SLO breaches via console alerts + high-level signals (latency P95, 5xx spike, queue length) and log incident channel. Triage owner collects affected regions, impacted clusters, and estimate of affected tenants.

2) Scoped impact verification: Run tenant-sample queries against each candidate cluster to validate desync/kvs issues. Use 'kv-check' script (internal) to surface mismatched prefix counts and highest-latency shards.

3) Quarantine strategy selection: Decide between node-level drain, availability-zone slice, or full-region partial drain based on observed error domains and capacity headroom in sibling regions. Prefer slice drains (<=25% traffic) when KV inconsistency observed to preserve cache hotness.

4) Pre-change customer gating: For Dedicated tenants with reserved capacity, notify account SRE and apply circuit-breaker exemptions. Mark Hosted customers in console route rules as 'susceptible' for follow-up communications.

5) Incremental traffic shift: Change routing in 3 stages with 5-10 minute observation windows: (A) Shift 10% of traffic to fallback region/model variant; (B) If stable, shift additional 30%; (C) Continue in 20-30% increments until target. Monitor per-tenant error and latency, abort if error rate > baseline+3x for >2 minutes.

6) KV cache reconciliation: After traffic migration, run cache sync checks for tenants that experienced cold-start regressions. If heavy miss rate persists, trigger targeted shard warming using recorded prefix snapshots.
7) Model fallback policy: Where quantization/variant fallback is used, ensure deterministic selection by model family and length. Log fallback reasons and tag traces for downstream QA/eval.
8) Stabilize and observe: Keep elevated telemetry dashboards open for at least 90 minutes post-migration and run synthetic acceptance tests across 20 representative tenants.
9) Reintroduce drained slices gradually: Only reintroduce once KV health metrics return to baseline and error budgets are stable for 30 minutes. Prefer reintroduction in reverse order of evacuation.
10) Post-incident: Create a customer-facing summary, run an internal technical debrief, and open follow-up engineering tasks for root-cause patches.
11) Emergency rollback: If evacuation fails or downstream systems degrade, execute the rollback plan (see rollback_plan field) and escalate to the on-call lead and customer success.
12) Runbook owner check: After play completes, runbook owner posts status and next steps into the incident channel and updates this doc with timestamps and PR links.

13) Escalation decision points: Clear thresholds listed for when to engage Executive SLA team (sustained customer error rate >5% over 15 minutes) and when to open a dedicated support war room for high-value tenants.

14) Dedicated-specific note: For Dedicated pools with isolated routing, coordinate change windows with customer maintenance preferences; if immediate action needed, require account SRE sign-off for tenant-affecting changes.
rollback_plan: Primary rollback mechanism: revert routing changes in reverse order within the console routing UI and re-enable any previously paused capacity groups. Rollback steps: 1) Pause all in-flight route reassignments. 2) Reapply original route table snapshot (console stores snapshots per incident). 3) Warm target clusters by spinning up 10% additional capacity for 10 minutes if necessary. 4) If rollback stalls due to KV mismatch, initiate targeted cache purge + refill for affected tenants. Abort conditions: inability to restore error rate to baseline within 20 minutes — escalate to SRE manager and consider cross-region failover protocols.
communications: Internal - Slack template: @incident when initiating evacuation: '[INCIDENT] Region X partial outage: starting targeted evacuation stage 1 -> shifting 10% traffic to Region Y. Observability owners please confirm dashboards. Assigned: <assignee>. ETA per stage: 5-10m.'

Customer-facing status page copy: 'We are investigating elevated errors affecting requests from Region X. Traffic is being incrementally routed to healthy regions. Some requests may have higher latency for a short period. We will post updates every 15 minutes. Impact: potential delays and transient errors. Mitigation: routing to alternate region.'

Dedicated account email template (short): 'We detected instability impacting your dedicated capacity in Region X. We are executing a controlled traffic migration to a healthy region. We expect minimal disruption; your account manager will reach out. For rollback preference or maintenance window constraints, reply to this message.'
Support playbook note: include list of top-20 affected tenants by request volume and assign 1 support contact per high-volume tenant for proactive outreach.
notes_and_decisions: 2026-03-10 - Initial triage: Determined root cause likely internal KV lease expiration causing regional desync. Decided to attempt incremental traffic shift rather than immediate full-region failover to preserve cache hotness.
2026-03-11 - Decision: Use 10/40/50 traffic-step plan to reduce cold-start cost and allow prewarming. Liam to validate reheating script before first shift.

2026-03-12 - Trade-off noted: aggressive shifts reduce customer-visible errors faster but increase cold-start token costs. Team accepted cost trade-off for P0 incidents until runtime-1.22 hotfix ships.
2026-03-13 - Temporary mitigation deployed: KV lease refresher turned on for critical shards; observed 30% reduction in 5xx for sampled tenants.
2026-03-14 - In-progress: Running stage 1 traffic shift to Region Y; monitoring for per-tenant error spikes. Next update expected 2026-03-14T10:30Z.
